sections.title: Building bigger numbers
sections.content: A1 gave you nulla-tíz and the round tens — húsz, harminc, negyven, ötven, hatvan, hetven, nyolcvan, kilencven, száz — but not the numbers in between, which you need constantly for prices. 11-19 are built with tizen- plus the digit: tizen + egy = tizenegy (11), tizen + öt = tizenöt (15). Everything from 21 up is just tens-word + digit, no space: harminckettő (32), kilencvenhét (97). The only irregular part is the 20s, which use huszon- instead of húsz-: huszonegy (21), not húszegy. ezer ("thousand") is new too, and works the same way — kétezer (2000), ötezer (5000).

items.english: Her daughter is fifteen years old.
There are twenty-one sweaters in the store.

sections.content: két, not kettő, is the form you already use before a noun (két gyerek, "two children") — the same shortening happens with 12: tizenkét pulóver, not tizenkettő pulóver. Higher numbers ending in 2 (huszonkettő, harminckettő...) are fine standing alone, but this course sticks to tizenkét and két when a number sits directly in front of a noun.
